records.title: Bearframe RPG uses 32x32 world tiles; older 48px World Editor format is separate
records.summary: Current Founder-selected Bearframe RPG terrain/collision grid is 32x32; purchased/collected tile assets must not be resized to 48px. A historical 384x768 sheet with 48px cells belongs to a separate World Editor v1 legacy contract and must not override this engine. Sprite frames may be taller than collision cells.

records.title: Bearframe runtime terrain tilesheet geometry
records.source: Founder-defined Bearframe World Editor v1 production standard
records.summary: World Editor v1 runtime tilesheets are 384 by 768 pixels using an 8 by 16 grid of 48 by 48 pixel tiles. Use top-left origin, exactly 128 slots, RGBA PNG, clean transparency, and no labels, gaps, or resizing. Preserve stable tile IDs and order.

records.source: Founder art feedback in Round24 continuation 2026-11-12; private assets excluded

Each diagonal needs its own perspective-aware poses and registered feet; rotating whole sprites or replaying one standing view is not an accepted walk. Preserve canonical identity and asymmetric armor. Establish eight-direction static geometry before expanding gait cycles; static coverage must never be reported as eight complete animated directions.

records.title: Four Sleeper sprites incorporate individualized Echo Frame visual traits without changing portrait identity

Preserve four original selection portraits and one-to-one corresponding sprites with distinct A violet neutral, B damaged scarf violet, C ponytail violet and D cyan worn identifiers. Treat Echo-style cues as deliberate layering on the existing approved look, NOT a new claim that the Sleeper starters are literally Echo Frames; do not blanket-damage or merge identities. Finish/validate 4-view static sprite construction before visual glitch/walk animations and Android engine save/selection testing. No private artwork uploaded publicly.

records.title: Four Sleepers need Echo-style system malfunction animations, no visual redesign

Keep all four original selection portraits and matching playable sprite silhouettes, palettes, armor, wear, and clothing exactly as approved. Once ordinary standing/idle/walk sprites are validated, create SEPARATE triggered or occasional animation clips for core light glitches, visor/side-display faults, short actuator stutters, brief desync/freeze, and recovery to idle. Keep readable native pixel scale, clean root/foot anchors, distinct purple/cyan lighting, restrained timings, and character-specific motion. This is not proof the characters are canonically Echo Frames. Do not upload user character art to the public repo.

records.title: Ghost Grid and Echo Frame ancient deterioration canon
records.source: Founder-approved Bearframe RPG reference images and art-direction corrections, Nov 2026
records.summary: Ghost Grid constructs are ancient advanced machines with accumulated age, heavy wear, overgrowth, and mechanical faults. Echo Frames are distinct old Ghost Grid-era sentient Frames, often humanoid or hulking with layered armor, exposed systems, torn fabric, and individualized silhouettes. They are weathered and overgrown too, with conspicuous glitches, memory/display instability, actuator failures, and unpredictable motion. Character reference sheets for Fract, Relay, Ruin, Murmur, and Bastion guide appearance. Broken details must be intentional and readable, not shortcuts for poor sprite anatomy.

records.title: Anchored stance test for six-leg pixel-art rigs
records.source: Original 12-frame Pillow exercise and local automated checks (2026-11-10); Saint11 pixel-art tutorials https://saint11.org/blog/pixel-art-tutorials/ ; Bearframe Warehouse existing Palinode gait record
records.summary: In a 12-frame 160x112 RGBA Pillow mechanics exercise, six indexed legs were rendered with alternating tripod groups; each frame had exactly three stance legs, planted feet used fixed screen-space anchors while the body translated, and eight physical archive-ring panel markers changed position around a fixed pylon. Validation passed leg counts, stance counts, transparency and ring movement; this does NOT prove natural gait, anatomy, silhouette separation or canon fidelity. Earlier leg drills tested static hip anchors; this exercise changes to moving hips plus anchored stance contacts. Limitation: swing trajectories jump at wraparound, far-side legs overlap, ring is schematic. Reproduce using explicit phase=(frame/N + tripod_offset) mod 1, stance phase<0.5, and compare native 1x frames before approval.

records.title: Bearframe pixel-art production quality gates
records.summary: Four independent gates: static anatomical and portrait-fidelity visual approval, real planted-foot and secondary motion, lossless 32px-compatible RGBA sheet/atlas QA, and installed Android landscape/save verification. PNG metadata pass does not equal artistic pass. Document fail conditions and reproducible evidence requirements.

records.title: Comprehensive Bearframe pixel-art discipline research
records.summary: Nov 11 sourced study covers native cluster drawing, anatomy, 4-direction consistency, real foot-contact gait, mechanical motion, canon identity, palettes, lighting, terrain autotiles, effects, UI, export and alpha/nearest render. Negative benchmark is prior warped/blurry walk. This is research, not production art approval.

records.title: Comprehensive Bearframe visual-art training checklist
records.source: Founder correction to Auren pixel-art study scope, Nov 2026
records.summary: Character design is ADDITIONAL homework, not a replacement for existing pixel-art work. Train and evaluate all competencies together: native-scale pixel placement and cluster discipline, clean contours, anatomy and proportions, distinctive and appealing character/portrait design, shape language, strong silhouettes, expressive face/visor/helmet design, readable armor and materials, lighting and color, frame-by-frame animation timing and movement weight, articulated mechanical geometry, natural accumulated overgrowth and age/damage, and intentional Ghost Grid mechanical faults versus distinctive Echo Frame glitch behavior. Compare original reference designs to native-resolution sprites and portraits; document failures, revisions, and objective QC before production approval. Previous rough assets are practice only, not finished.

records.title: Four starter selectable frames readability and Unit09 anatomy correction
records.summary: Audited four user-provided 1774x887 RGBA starter sheets (front, left, right, back each). View heights vary within each sheet by only 2-11px, useful for consistency, but 295k-343k distinct RGBA values and soft partial alpha on >99.9% of visible pixels show these are high-resolution 32-bit-STYLE references, NOT clean limited-palette native sprites. At 96px diagnostic sizes, armor details disappear; silhouette, visor color and mantle/ponytail carry identity. Independently rebuilt elongated hips/thighs/knees/shins/boots on earlier original Unit09 study (128x216 to 128x262, binary alpha); proportions improve yet armor/boots remain crude, so artistic quality gate FAILS. Next lock runtime pixel scale, establish one full-body native static art benchmark, check four-view foot anchors and test selectable characters at actual game scale before animation. User-supplied images never copied to public warehouse.

records.title: LibreSprite Round 09 verified four-layer three-frame static editing and art critique
records.summary: GitHub Actions run 42962709703 succeeded: LibreSprite 1.3 opened a public-safe generic 72x112 native RGBA practice ASE containing internal_structure, faceted_armor, drapery and signals layers over three frames, edited actual cels via JS and exported ASE, PNG sheet, JSON metadata and GIF. Validator passed stable feet y=101..111, no partial alpha, 14 colors including transparency. Independent parse of exported source and edited ASE verified all named layers, exact matching PNG composites and 14/15/16 source-to-editor pixel changes across frames 0/1/2 without modifying alpha. This is technically reproducible but VISUAL QUALITY FAILED: figure stiff, angular armor simplistic, helmet and materials lack refined character design. Continue actual editorial practice, not generic effects or premature game production.

records.title: Native pixel-art training and quality gate
records.source: Founder-requested study and corrections from Bearframe asset sessions
records.summary: Produce pixel art with actual raster or pixel editing tools, not an AI generated image as substitute. Evaluate at native resolution, check silhouettes, topology, consistent pixel size and every required limb, then compare passes before accepting a base animation frame.

records.title: Native scale and complete sprite anatomy
records.source: Founder feedback on previous Bearframe pixel-art attempts
records.summary: Evaluate sprites at native pixel resolution before enlarging them. Avoid blocky oversized pixels that obscure the silhouette. Check that full limb anatomy is present, including both legs where the design requires them. Review readability and proportions before treating a sprite as a locked base frame.

records.title: Palinode six leg gait evaluation
records.source: Bearframe pixel-art study assignment and prior exercise feedback
records.summary: Practice an articulated six-leg mechanical walking loop with distinct legs and alternating tripod support and swing phases. Check leg endpoints frame by frame, contact timing, silhouette and missing limb artifacts. Treat previous attempts as exercises, not finished production assets.

records.title: Relay portrait round 06 shape hierarchy lesson
records.summary: In a native 144x144 Relay portrait experiment, rebuilding the asymmetric torn hood, tilted CRT face, separated broken halo and scarf as large silhouette clusters before damage/detail improved reference identity compared with a prior symmetrical frontal round. Integer-pixel Pillow edits used 25 colors and binary alpha; validation confirms file structure, NOT artistic quality. Remaining weaknesses: overly rounded CRT, weak shoulder planes, thin overgrowth, and display-only glitches. Next practice: sharper 3/4 faceted CRT, stronger shoulder anatomy, organic seam growth, and true-motion studies.

records.title: Relay portrait Round 07 silhouette and perspective failure analysis
records.summary: Native 208x208 hand-authored Relay portrait study used 29-color palette and binary RGBA alpha; separate silhouette, faceted CRT/material, and sparse age passes; tested alternative broken-halo placements. Compared with Round 06, the CRT is more oblique and layer hierarchy clearer, but the silhouette still merges halo and hood near the top, shoulders remain shallow, and the design is not production quality. Technical PNG validation is not artistic validation. Next: three tiny monochrome thumbnail silhouettes, negative-space test at 1x, and focused 3/4 CRT/hood construction BEFORE lighting, overgrowth or glitches. Keep all prior animation and degeneration subjects in parallel.

records.title: Relay R09 angular hood and CRT geometry study
records.summary: Native 104x128 silhouettes retain Round08 B ring, zero overlap, 1 connected body each, gap 8.06/8.94/8.06px; two 116x104 CRT plane studies. Technical pass only; artistic quality unverified. Four portrait-matched Sleepers remain production priority; no extra permanent damage.

records.title: Relay Round 08 silhouette separation versus character appeal
records.summary: Three native 104x128 integer-pixel silhouette studies compared broken relay-ring placement while holding Relay's body constant. A/B/C ring-to-body minimum gaps were 2.83/3.61/4.00 pixels with no direct overlap. B better isolates the left rim, C is top-heavy; these numerical tests check geometry but NOT artistic quality. A separate 112x100 angled CRT material-plane exercise was also completed. All designs still fail canonical character-art review because hood/head and shoulders remain generic/rounded; further angular asymmetrical silhouette and 3/4 perspective practice is required before effects or animation. Preserve this critical failure along with the evidence and continue the other study subjects.

records.title: Relay Round 6 portrait failure and art-method correction
records.source: Founder direct visual critique of Relay portrait Round 6, Nov 2026
records.summary: Founder quality feedback: the Relay Round 6 portrait resembles crude MS Paint drawing and is not a polished or sufficiently faithful Echo Frame design. Basic programmatic circles, polygons, flat fills, and added surface speckles are not a substitute for strong character-design fundamentals. Corrective workflow: study canonical Relay reference; establish an appealing, asymmetrical perspective-correct head and strong silhouette; build helmet/CRT display/hood and armor in meaningful layered planes; place and revise pixel clusters deliberately; verify visual fidelity at native resolution on light and dark backgrounds; only after the still image succeeds add wear, moss, corruption, or animation. Preserve all existing animation, overgrowth, silhouette and glitch training. Treat this pass as an unsuccessful quality-gate attempt and retain critique rather than celebrating minor metrics.

records.title: Round 18 four-view starter reference adaptation and ASE verification
records.summary: Prepared Vera's existing Starter A turnaround as FOUR independently aligned 128x256 source-derived RGBA sprite views, sharing a 74-color opaque palette, hard alpha, matching y=248 soles and top y=11, exported a 512x256 four-direction sheet and constructed a 4-frame/3-layer 32bpp ASE. Independently parsed every ASE cel and verified lossless compositing matches the four PNGs. This does NOT represent new hand-drawn character art, an animation, a LibreSprite-open test of this specific proprietary file, or production-ready sprites. The source images and derived assets remain private in conversation downloads; only method/metrics are public. Next study should tackle genuinely independent pixel-art armor design; keep all former animation/glitch/overgrowth coursework.

records.title: Sleeper Unit 09 manual static sprite construction failed quality gate
records.summary: Independently authored an original 128x216 static front-standing Unit09 sprite using 16 hand-planned opaque RGB colors and binary 0/255 alpha, complete arms/legs, visor, head-side modules, red wiring and an 09 shoulder mark. This was FROM BLANK PIXELS and is distinct from the separate reference-crop/palette exercise. Comparison with the supplied canonical sprite shows legs too short and stout, insufficiently layered torso plates and weak volumetric helmet construction. Technical PNG validity is not professional artistry; this remains a failing construction sketch. Next: correct hips/thigh/shin proportions and interlocking armor at 1x before animation or damage.

records.title: Starter Sleeper Unit 09 reference and palette study
records.summary: Founder shifted introductory character study from complex Relay to starter Sleeper Frame Unit 09. The supplied source has strong bone-white angular helmet and chest plates, narrow violet visor, 09-marked shoulder, dark understructure, red cabling, distinctive knees and boots. A 125x321 front standing figure was isolated transparently from the supplied pixel-style sheet and placed in a 160x352 transparent frame. Global 64-color reduction loses purple emissive accents; reserving an 8-color violet ramp then tuning its brightness/saturation preserves the identity. Original source remains benchmark. This was an EXTRACTED REFERENCE AND COLOR STUDY, not new hand-drawn pixel art or production approval. Next must paint the helmet and shoulders from a blank canvas with deliberate clusters and compare at 1x before a full sprite or animation.

records.title: Unit09 two shin-section rebuild attempts reject promotion

Critical provenance: latest hourly v4b checkpoint was NOT available in active chat, so A/B are isolated practice and MUST NOT replace v4b or be called the new best. Next priority is reopening actual v4b then resolving knee/shin/ankle form with a real skeleton/section edit. No user art uploaded publicly.

records.title: LibreSprite 1.3 real native pixel editor successfully verified in GitHub Actions
records.summary: Implemented a reproducible GitHub Actions workflow that downloads the OFFICIAL LibreSprite 1.3 AppImage, extracts and launches its actual headless batch editor, executes JavaScript inside a sprite cel to change two RGBA pixels, exports a PNG and validates those exact pixels plus transparency. All steps passed on run 42961553641 with downloadable image/report artifacts. This is a VERIFIED TOOL INTEGRATION smoke test, NOT an artistic quality or game production pass. LibreSprite is ephemeral per runner; current ChatGPT sandbox does not have a local editor install. Use this workflow to build future authored layered sprite and animation tests, and keep source game art out of public repo.
